correctness.rationale: All six-term possibilities are excluded by \(115/231<1/2\) for the six smallest squarefree semiprimes. Positivity forces the prefix cutoffs 31 (seven terms) and 63 (eight terms), leaving exactly 21 and 18564 possibilities. The exact factorization \((ax-b)(ay-b)=b^2\) covers every unrestricted final integer pair and the certificate enumerates every positive divisor of \(b^2\). Both independent exact implementations find zero admissible seven/eight-term solutions. The nine-term witness is verified by Fraction arithmetic and exact primality checks.

An unindexed exact numerical computation is a residual originality risk.

value.rationale: The least number of allowed reciprocal terms is the sharp natural cardinality invariant for the simplest nonintegral target in Erdős Problem #306, whose general existence was recently settled. An exact nine-term lower-and-upper-bound classification is a substantive concrete benchmark for quantitative versions of that theorem; the full divisor-bound proof makes it more than arbitrary small-number enumeration. No general-target extrapolation is asserted.
